column3: NASB follows the critical text; it renders “were teaching” as “began teaching” and “brothers” as “brethren.”
NASB follows the critical text; “no small commotion” is rendered “great dissension,” and it supplies “the brethren” as the subject of “determined.”
NASB renders “sent forward” as “sent on their way.”
NASB follows the critical text; “how much” is rendered “all that.”
NASB renders “command” as “direct” and “keep” as “observe.”
NASB follows the critical text; “to understand” is rendered “to look into.”
NASB follows the critical text; “Men brothers” is rendered “Brethren,” and “chose” is “made a choice.”
NASB follows the critical text without the second “to them”; it adds “He also did.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB renders “testing God” as “put God to the test” and adds “placing.”
NASB follows the critical text without “Christ.”
NASB renders “how much” as “what” and reorders the verse.
NASB renders “being silent” as “stopped speaking” and “Men brothers” as “Brethren.”
NASB follows the critical text; “visited” is rendered “concerned Himself about.”
Close to the Greek.
The quotation is in capitals except “I will return”; “the ruined things” is rendered “ITS RUINS,” and “set upright” is “RESTORE.”
NASB follows the critical text; it ends the verse at “MY NAME” and carries “says the Lord, who does these things” into v. 18.
NASB follows the critical text without the Textus Receptus words “known to God are all His works”; it carries over “SAYS THE LORD” from v. 17 and renders “known from eternity” as “KNOWN FROM OF OLD.”
NASB renders “I judge” as “it is my judgment.”
NASB follows the critical text; “pollutions of the idols” is rendered “things contaminated by idols,” and “sexual immorality” is “fornication.”
NASB adds “since.”
NASB follows the critical text; it renders “choose” as an infinitive and reorders the verse.
NASB follows the critical text with “the brethren who are elders” instead of “and the brethren”; it supplies “they sent this letter.”
NASB follows the critical text without the Textus Receptus words “saying, Be circumcised and keep the law”; “minds” is rendered “souls.”
NASB follows the critical text; it renders “with one accord” as “having become of one mind.”
NASB renders “handed over” as “risked.”
NASB renders “are telling” as “will also report.”
NASB follows the critical text; “no further burden” is rendered “no greater burden,” and “necessary things” is “essentials.” A full-width colon appears in the NASB text.
NASB follows the critical text; “sexual immorality” is rendered “fornication,” and “keeping yourselves” is “keep yourselves free.” A stray quotation mark appears in the NASB text.
NASB follows the critical text (“went down”); “multitude” is rendered “congregation.”
